core_obligations: The bounded below case (proof lines 7065-7068): if the first complex of the resolution vanishes in degrees below some integer t, the assertion follows immediately from the cited lemma on double complexes with the roles of the two indices exchanged.

Reduction by truncation (proof lines 7069-7078): for every integer t the sequence of stupid truncations is again an exact complex of complexes, with associated double complex A(t); every cohomology class of the total complex of A is the image of a class of the total complex of A(t) for a suitable t, as one sees by looking at explicit representatives.

Surjectivity and injectivity (proof lines 7079-7086): the previous step shows that each cohomology class of the target comes from the cohomology of the truncated resolved complex, which gives surjectivity of the map on cohomology; injectivity follows because for every t the corresponding map of truncated complexes is injective and by the same kind of argument.
proof_roadmap: Settle the case where the resolution is bounded below by the companion lemma.
Truncate the resolution to reduce an arbitrary cohomology class to a bounded below situation.
Conclude surjectivity and injectivity of the map on cohomology.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the map from a complex of abelian groups to the total complex of a resolution of it is a quasi-isomorphism, with no boundedness assumption on the resolution (statement lines 7053-7063). The proof is a complete argument: the bounded below case is attributed to the companion lemma on double complexes (proof lines 7065-7068); in general the resolution is truncated in degrees at least t, every cohomology class of the total complex is shown to come from the total complex of a truncation by examining explicit representatives, which yields surjectivity (proof lines 7069-7082); and injectivity is obtained from the injectivity of the truncated maps (proof lines 7083-7086). The non-formal content is the truncation argument transferring an arbitrary class into a bounded below situation. The claim is H2: a structured argument with each input named.
